Length of intensive care unit and hospital stay

Post-operative stay (total and ICU) was comparable in both groups, with no statistically signi fi cant difference (total: non-fasting 1.9 + 2.6 days vs. fasting 1.6 + 1.3 days, P = 0.36; ICU: non-fasting 0.06 + 0.42 days vs. fasting 0.01 + 0.10 days, P = 0.55).

Thirty-day chest infection rate and incidence of procedural-related deaths

Symptoms of respiratory infections were reported in three patients within 30 days post-procedure; one patient in each group had a common cold, and one patient in the fasting group was treated for pneumonia without sequelae ( P = 0.999). No procedural-related death occurred.

Discussion

This study showed that a non-fasting strategy is advantageous compared with a fasting strategy regarding patient ' s well-being and comparable in terms of safety for patients undergoing elective CIED procedures. To our knowledge, this is the fi rst randomized clinical study to assess the bene fi ts of a non-fasting strategy for an interventional cardiac procedure. The summed pre-procedural well-being score was signi fi cantly lower for the non-fasting group, which re fl ects more well-being in this group which was mainly driven by signi fi cantly lower scores for hunger and tiredness in the non-fasting group. Non-fasting before CIED procedures did not in fl uence renal, metabolic, and haematological blood parameters and duration of hospital stay.
